service.description:
Extract NetSuite sales orders for a reconciliation window over SuiteQL (REST Web Services), writing normalized JSON to the automation data-manager folder. Same in/out contract and same on-disk {records, metadata} file shape as the OMS and Shopify getters, so the automation edge and the Spark compare stage are unchanged (DAR-BE-032).
TRANSPORT: SuiteQL, not a SuiteScript RESTlet. Measured against a live account on 2026-09-02: 1000 rows per page (the documented ceiling, honoured) at ~880 rows/sec, so a 161k-order month enumerates in about three minutes. A RESTlet would additionally require a script record, a deployment and a role grant inside the CLIENT's production NetSuite and buys nothing for a presence check. No NetSuite-side deployment is needed for this service.
CREDENTIAL: the existing NsAuthConfig OAuth2 M2M profile, whose scope already defaults to "restlets rest_webservices". The SuiteQL endpoint host is derived from that profile's tokenUrl, so the account id is never configured twice and the request URL stays inside OutboundHttpPolicy's allow-list by construction.
POPULATION AND PROJECTION ARE CONFIGURATION (DAR-BE-044), not constants in the extractor. The record type, the table, the window column and the column-to-record-field mapping all come from the NsSuiteQlSourceQuery named by nsSuiteQlSourceQueryId. That is what lets one connector row serve every NetSuite pair, including the within-NetSuite pairs, instead of minting a systemEnumId, a connector row and an extract service per endpoint.
JOIN KEY: for the OMS order-presence pair the emitted orderId carries NetSuite's custbody_hc_order_id — the column the HotWax integration itself writes — so a match means "this NetSuite order came from that OMS order" rather than "these two strings are equal". Orders keyed in directly in NetSuite carry no such value; when the query declares an originFieldName every record also carries it (HOTWAX or NETSUITE_NATIVE) so those can be excluded by a configured rule, because an exclusion rule cannot match an absent field.
KEEP (DAR-BE-318 plan 3b-2b, rulings 3b2b-12 and 3b2b-23): this read filters nothing. A run's source filters and NetSuite's built-in drop run once, in Spark, over the file this writes, and Spark writes the side file of what they set aside. That is why the service declares no filter parameter (the NETSUITE_SUITEQL row's filterParameterName, sourceFilters, now only says the endpoint takes Keep). The built-in drop: a SALES_LINES line with no HotWax line id (a store-credit payment line) is written with nsUnkeyedLine "Y", after any keepRecordFields projection, and the row's declared Keep line (data/NetSuiteConnectorSeedData.xml, keepLinesJson) sets it aside as "0:orderLineId". Which unkeyed lines are read at all stays a read-side limit in the query (payment lines only).
WINDOW: NetSuite's trandate is DATE-granular and stored in the account's timezone, so the window is applied as half-open [windowStart, windowEnd) on whole days. Give day-aligned windows; a sub-day window will not narrow the result.

parameter.name: nsSuiteQlSourceQueryId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned NsSuiteQlSourceQuery identifier. Says which NetSuite population this side enumerates (record type, table, window column) and how its columns map onto reconciliation record fields, and carries the NsAuthConfig that supplies the OAuth2 M2M credential and — via its tokenUrl host — the SuiteQL endpoint. Before DAR-BE-044 this parameter was the auth config directly and the population was hardcoded, which is why every new NetSuite pair needed a new service.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the window (inclusive); accepts Timestamp, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, epoch millis or yyyy-MM-dd. Reduced to a whole date. Required unless lookupKeys is given.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the window, EXCLUSIVE — an order dated exactly at the bound belongs to the next window, so consecutive chunks do not double-count their boundary. Required unless lookupKeys is given.

parameter.name: windowFieldName
parameter.description: DAR-BE-318 plan 3b-1 (ruling 3b1-4). What the window bounds. Blank, or the query row's own dateColumn: the window applies to that column, exactly as every run read does. darpanStamp: a dataset's daily read, by what changed (RECORDS and SALES_LINES queries only): the transactions whose header lastmodifieddate or any of whose lines' linelastmodifieddate is at or after windowStart's day, with no end, so what changed today is read too. Any other value is refused. No default on purpose: a run side names none, so a kept copy is never cut on a field this service picked for it.

parameter.name: datasetRead
parameter.description: DAR-BE-318 plan 3b-1. True on every read that builds a dataset's kept copy (the NETSUITE_SUITEQL row's datasetReadParametersJson sends it, data/NetSuiteConnectorSeedData.xml): each record carries darpanStamp, the later of its header lastmodifieddate and its newest line's linelastmodifieddate as a UTC instant; a read on the dateColumn ends the day after windowEnd, so today's transactions are in it; and a query on any template but RECORDS or SALES_LINES is refused, so a dataset on one fails its first read and never builds a copy. The dataset's windowField is the query's dateColumn (e.g. trandate) and its stampField darpanStamp; a SALES_LINES dataset's idField is a header key plus lineId (e.g. tranId,lineId), since lineId numbers a line within its own order.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-118 / DAR-BE-119. A read by key: only the records whose lookupKeyField holds one of these (at most 1000; letters, digits, # _ . -), with no window, still under the query row's own conditions. A conclusion lookup asks by internalId; a re-check of an older audit finding by its compare key. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending keys, so a connector without it is never asked for a whole window instead.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of; one of the query's fields.

parameter.name: conclusionLookup
parameter.description: DAR-BE-318 (plan 3b-2b, ruling 3b2b-12). Sent by a conclusion lookup (RunConclusionStep), which reads by key and compares nothing, so no Spark Keep follows it: with lookupKeys, a SALES_LINES read then leaves out the lines with no HotWax line id, as every read did before Keep moved into Spark. A run's read by the other side's keys and an audit re-check send none: they are kept in Spark like any run read.

parameter.name: changedSince
parameter.description: DAR-BE-320. An audit's daily read, instead of the whole window: the window's records (the query's dateColumn in [windowStart, windowEnd), as a run reads) that could have moved since this instant's day, whole orders: the header or any line changed (lastmodifieddate, linelastmodifieddate), dated from that day on, an order with a keyed line in one of the query's liveLineStates, or an order HotWax wrote one of the query's omsChangedStatusIds item statuses for since then (asked of HotWax first, at most 1000). Only a RECORDS or SALES_LINES query over transaction with nothing read off other transactions can be read so; one asking HotWax for item statuses only with omsChangedStatusIds; one counting HotWax shipments never. Any other, a read by key, or windowFieldName darpanStamp is refused before any request, and the audit then reads that check's whole window. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending it.

parameter.name: lookupWithinWindow
parameter.description: DAR-BE-156. A read by key that also keeps windowStart/windowEnd: an audit re-check of its older findings reads what the check's full read would, restricted to the keys, so the date index bounds it.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to netsuite-orders-{from}-{thru}.json.

parameter.name: pageSize
parameter.description: Optional page size, capped at NetSuite's SuiteQL ceiling of 1000. A larger request is capped server-side anyway, which would otherwise make a caller believe it had read further than it had.

parameter.name: keepRecordFields
parameter.description: Optional projection: top-level record fields to keep in the output file. nsUnkeyedLine is written after it, so narrowing the output cannot disable the built-in Keep line. The connector no longer drives this — since DAR-BE-044 the field mapping IS the projection, exactly as the SELECT list is for DATABASE — but a direct caller may still narrow.

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id for progress heartbeats. Advisory only.

parameter.name: progressStageCode
parameter.description: Which extract stage this run is: EXTRACT_FILE1 or EXTRACT_FILE2. Defaults to EXTRACT_FILE2.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total, which adds a progress percent alongside the count.

service.description: DAR-BE-318 (rulings P3b1-6, P3b1-9). The NetSuite side of darpan's kept-copy projection: it refuses every side, so a NetSuite run reads live. Served parity is not proven on the real record shape: a copy record carries darpanStamp, which the live record does not; a query's derived columns (linked children, line sums, locations) and HotWax statuses are read at read time and move neither stamp; and SuiteQL compares days in the account's zone. Named by the NETSUITE_SUITEQL row (data/NetSuiteConnectorSeedData.xml), so giving that row a window field can never start serving a copy. Reads nothing.

set.value: a NetSuite side reads live: its copy's records carry darpanStamp, and the columns a query derives from other records at read time move neither stamp
